A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Flat-LoRA and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched. V1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A–E are included in this comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original T5-base and CLIP fine-tuning results, comparisons with LoRA variants, and rank-sensitivity experiments in Tables 1–3 and Figure 2.

after.justification: V2 retains original fine-tuning experiments and adds LLM, image-generation, distribution-shift, efficiency and appendix results.

M1.justification: The Bayesian expected-loss objective, filter-scaled Gaussian perturbations and seed-based reconstruction remain unchanged. Appendix C introduces an all-layer variant that additionally perturbs normalization parameters, biases and embeddings using absolute-weight-based noise. This extends the procedure without replacing the core method.

E1.justification: The GLUE and image-classification coverage is retained. V2 adds WizardLM/MT-Bench dialogue evaluation, MetaMathQA/GSM8K mathematics, CodeFeedback/HumanEval coding, 3D Icons text-to-image generation, CIFAR-100-C corruptions, and Alpaca/InstructEval instruction following. These substantially expand task and distribution-shift coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds AdaLoRA to the retained CoLA/MRPC comparison, SAM applied to adapter versus full weights in Table 6, and oBAR, nBAR, LoRA-Pro, GaLore and CorDA in Appendix E. These are evaluated comparators absent from v1's corresponding experiments, rather than merely new citations.

E3.justification: V2 introduces Llama 2 and SDXL training protocols, GPT-4 first-turn scoring, PASS@1 evaluation, matched-seed image generation, corruption-severity testing and SAM-radius sweeps. For the retained CLIP experiment, the stated full-fine-tuning learning rate changes from 0.00001 to 0.0001 despite identical Table 2 scores. This establishes a reported setting revision, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The rank sweep is retained. V2 adds corruption robustness, adapter-space versus full-space perturbation controls, resource measurements and loss-landscape visualizations. Appendices A–D add training/test-loss and generalization-gap curves, perturbation-component diagnostics, an all-layer perturbation ablation, and noise-strength sensitivity across model sizes.

E5.justification: V2 adds shaded variability bands to the retained rank plots, changing v1 Figure 2 into v2 Figure 5, although the band statistic is not explicitly defined. Three-trial mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged for the original classification experiments. The new image-generation comparison explicitly matches seeds across methods; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Several GLUE values change: rank-8 Flat-LoRA's CoLA score rises from 83.19 to 83.61, while LoRA changes from 82.20 to 82.87. LoRA-GA ranks below LoRA on both datasets in v1 Table 3 but above it in v2 Table 5. V2 also adds substantial LLM, generation, robustness, efficiency and appendix results. Table 2's image-classification values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds the LoRA-SAM full-weight perturbation expansion and approximation in Equations 3–4 and the attributed smoothing Lemma 3.1. It also revises the forward-variance derivation to include nonzero input means and states Proposition 3.2. These substantially extend v1's short mathematical justification without changing the core noise rule.

C1.justification: V2 makes improvement under distribution shift an explicit central claim in its abstract, contributions and conclusion. V1 claimed effectiveness and state-of-the-art performance on NLP and image classification without this explicit out-of-domain scope. The central full-space-flatness and efficiency claims are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations connecting restricted-space SAM, landscape flatness, distribution-shift robustness and smaller generalization gaps. Appendix A attributes gains to generalization rather than lower training loss, and Appendix D supplies practical noise-strength guidance. V1's explanation that LoRA-GA may converge quickly to inferior local solutions is removed alongside revised comparator results.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code release; v2 states repository and supplementary-code availability, which cannot be independently verified from the PDFs. V2 adds LLM precision settings, sample counts, warmup, SDXL training details, SAM search ranges, and RTX 4090 memory/time measurements. However, v1's explicit GLUE weight-decay value is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against random-perturbation methods and LoRA variants, including Gaussian model perturbation, NoisyTune, LoRASC and BAR. It adds references supporting smoothing theory, new benchmarks and GaLore/CorDA comparisons, while dropping some earlier references. These changes extend beyond publication-status updates to retained citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations undergo extensive rewriting. Related work gains numbered subsections, integration comparisons and ablations receive separate experimental sections, and Appendices A–E are introduced. Terminology and front matter are also revised, including correcting 'Adaption' to 'Adaptation'.

P2.justification: V2 switches to a two-column conference layout, relocates existing displays and redraws the rank plots with shaded bands. It adds a method schematic, generated-image comparisons, corruption charts, landscape surfaces, diagnostic curves and multiple experimental tables. These substantially change the visual presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V1 supports its central flatness and efficiency arguments mainly indirectly. V2 adds direct SAM-space comparisons, landscape and generalization-gap diagnostics, and measured resource costs, substantially strengthening those arguments while testing larger models and distribution shifts. Reporting inconsistencies remain: Section 4.5 claims gains of 0.71 and 1.83 points, whereas Table 4 implies 0.92 and 2.23. These issues temper confidence in individual statements but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in validation.
